findings.title: Incorrect conditional expectation in the log-normal aspirin example
findings.claim: The displayed substitutions give E[Y|T] for the model in Eq1.
findings.suspect_step: Incorrect covariance coefficient, conditioning variance and missing logarithm of dose.

counterexample.assumptions: Independent Gaussian log-noises; a,b>0; positive variances; t=1,2 in positive support

repair.verification: Analytic Gaussian conditioning and independent numerical illustration

findings.counterevidence: Eq8 and the preceding Gaussian-conditioning identity are correct; Eq4 intervention result remains valid.
findings.supported_impact: Major at the claim level: the principal worked example contains a demonstrated wrong quantitative derivation, and an allowed-parameter instance reverses its observational dose trend. This is closely tied to the paper's explanatory contribution. The broad expressivity thesis and the surviving qualitative claims do not settle the severity.
findings.remaining_work: Plot/source provenance and regeneration if quantitative figures used the printed formula

severity_calibration.core_dependency: The abstract presents concrete causal examples as the demonstration of the paper's contribution. Section2 makes the aspirin model the running example, Section2.1 uses its observational response to distinguish prediction from intervention, and the p.3 continuation explicitly invokes Eq.(9). The failed substitution therefore belongs to the principal worked quantitative comparison.
assumptions_rechecked: Fixed model parameters, not a posterior average over parameter uncertainty
a,b>0; independent Gaussian log-noises; strictly positive variances
Doses t>0; the saved comparison doses lie in this support
The saved trend reversal has c=1>0; it does not establish reversal in the c=0 specialization
A dose-independent exponent constant cancels in the saved ratios; reinterpreting T as logged conflicts with Eq.(1) and does not correct the covariance coefficient
counterevidence_and_survivors: Eq.(8) and the preceding Gaussian-conditioning identity are correct.
At c=0 the corrected mean still increases with dose for a,b>0; the qualitative confounding example survives.
For c>0 the source asserts that positive association is possible, not universal. That existential statement survives the demonstrated reversal at another allowed parameter setting.
Eq.(4)/Appendix B.5's fixed-dose intervention mean remains valid.
No effect on the paper's plotted parameter setting, fitted parameters or empirical figures has been shown.

findings.title: Marginal equality extended incorrectly to parentless stochastic interventions
findings.claim: q(y)=q(y|t) for any intervention with empty new parent set.
findings.suspect_step: Parentless treatment randomization does not remove dependence of outcome on treatment.

counterexample.assumptions: Acyclic two-node DAG, positive support, unchanged outcome mechanism, empty new parent set

repair.statement: Average the parent-adjusted conditional over g(t), or restrict marginal equality to atomic intervention at the assigned treatment.
repair.verification: Exact law of total probability; finite rational table checked

findings.counterevidence: Atomic aspirin examples and Appendix I conditional reasoning remain valid.
findings.supported_impact: Major at the claim level: this is a failed advertised generalization of the core intervention-inference derivation, not a peripheral equality. It removes the intervention-distribution dependence from the desired stochastic-policy marginal. The valid atomic case is preserved separately.
findings.remaining_work: Author scope choice; no empirical consequence asserted

severity_calibration.core_dependency: Section2.3 defines general kernel replacement and refers readers to Appendix J for adjustment shortcuts. Appendix J explicitly asks for the outcome marginal q(y) in more general models and extends the atomic equality to every parentless intervention; Appendix C.1 supplies the purported proof. Dropping the policy weights answers a different query from that advertised marginal.
assumptions_rechecked: Acyclic two-node DAG T->Y, with Y not in the original parent set of T
Replacing the root-treatment distribution is permitted by Definition2.1
The new parent set is empty, with a nondegenerate assignment distribution
All observational and intervened joint cells are positive
The outcome mechanism is unchanged; no confounding, support failure or conditional-version ambiguity is used
counterevidence_and_survivors: The general joint factorization in Eq.(5) remains valid for stochastic interventions.
Appendix I Eq.(36) identifies the fixed-treatment conditional response on the intervention support.
For an atomic intervention the marginal equals the conditional at the assigned treatment value only; the main fixed-dose aspirin calculation survives.
The C.1 proof derives the conditional response, which does not establish the asserted stochastic marginal.

scope_clarifications.location: Definition3.2 pp7-8 and Appendix N.1 pp28-29
scope_clarifications.description: Full evidence and partial evidence differ; Appendix N retains the full posterior joint, so no extra failed counterfactual result is established.
